findings.title: Unstemmed component-manifest lineage tokens remain in prose
findings.finding: A whole-subject scan excluding artifact paths and recordedInputs found 39 prose occurrences of leftover-join.vN without a lineage stem across 20 fields. Examples include the landing histories in every findingDisposition entry, the cumulative landsNote, and the historical prose in basedOn.predecessorV6.role and basedOn.predecessorV8.role. The dispatch expressly attacks any unstemmed leftover-join.vN prose token, and this artifact itself distinguishes component-manifest, g15, and packaging lineages whose version numbers are unrelated.
findings.requiredRepair: In a successor, fully qualify every one of the 39 prose tokens with its actual lineage. These occurrences are component-manifest lineage history; retain already-correct g15 and packaging stems, change no digest, partition member, finding identifier, or landing fact, and do not edit any frozen predecessor.

findings.title: basedOn.d282.role retains a false current-at-draft-time claim
findings.finding: basedOn.d282.role says 'Current DR-103 leftover-join at draft time.' That was true for the predecessor artifact, but D-304 subsequently recorded component-manifest leftover-join.v12. The v13 registerRowNote, predecessorV12 role, and remeasurementClause correctly identify component-manifest leftover-join.v12 as current at this draft and component-manifest leftover-join.v9 as historical. The surviving D-282 sentence therefore creates two incompatible current joins inside one custody record.
